title: Provenance-aware evidence counting
purpose: Count the independent observations behind a claim by following each report back to its root observations, so relayed, echoed and merged reports are not counted twice, and simulate non-backtracking relaying between agents. A claim relayed A to B to C and back to A counts as one observation.

entry_points.name: count_independent_evidence
entry_points.arguments: reports: [{id, agent, claim, observed: bool, sources: [report ids of the same claim]}]
entry_points.returns: {claims: [{claim, reports, independent_observations, roots, unsupported_reports}], holdings: [{agent, claim, reports_held, independent_observations}]}

entry_points.name: relay_non_backtracking
entry_points.arguments: edges: [[sender, receiver]]; origins: {agent: [observation ids]}; rounds: 1 to 10000

assumptions: Every report either is a root observation or names the reports it rests on; the provenance links are complete and honest.
Two root observations are independent of each other; the tool cannot detect a shared hidden cause.
guarantees: The independent count is the number of distinct root observations reachable through sources; relaying, echoing and merging never increase it.
Reports whose sources never reach a root are listed as unsupported and contribute nothing.
In the relay, an agent ends up holding exactly the observations whose origin can reach it along directed edges, given enough rounds.

known_wrong.name: returning_claim_is_not_corroboration
known_wrong.why: Counting messages, a receives its own observation back and counts it as a second, corroborating one.

limits: Counts are only as good as the provenance links: a report that hides its sources looks like a new root observation. Root observations are treated as independent even when they share an unrecorded cause. Reports may only cite reports about the same claim. The relay is a synchronous round-based simulation for small graphs (thousands of edges) and does not model message loss or delay.
technique_references: Data incest and double counting in decentralized estimation
Non-backtracking message passing (belief propagation without echo)
